g_roast: Ladies and gentlemen, boys and girls, Tegan has flown in front of two hundred wedding guests in hats, and she's never once looked as nervous as she does watching you lot fight.
I've done school visits with forty seven year olds who listened better than this party, and one of them tried to eat a feather.
g_fire_back: Fair, cariad, that's a good one, and from the one who tried to stroke an owl that was clearly having a bad day.
Ha, duw, I deserved that, didn't I? Tegan thinks so too, look at her face.
g_pile_on: Oh, worse than that, boys and girls. They shouted in the woods, every bird for a mile left, and then came the question of why it was quiet.
Then at the inn it was hours of tracking, apparently. It was sat on a fence, waiting for them.
lines.g_peacemake: Shh, both of you, gently now, you're frightening the bird. Sit down, voices low, and say it again like you'd say it to a nervous hawk.
lines.g_take_side: I'm with {name} on this one, sorry. Tegan's been watching them all evening, and she's never wrong about people.
lines.g_left_out: Carry on, the pair of you, Tegan wants a fly up the ridge. She's been sat still too long.
lines.g_include: Come on, sit by me, there's room. Tegan won't mind, she's decided she likes you, and she's very fussy.
lines.g_bad_plan: Here's the plan, boys and girls. We all run into the woods shouting, as loud as we can, and see what jumps out.
lines.g_plan_yes: Tidy, quiet and careful, I like it. Tegan approves, look, she's settled.
lines.g_plan_no: No, cariad, that's a loud plan, and loud gets people hurt in the woods. Let's do it quieter, please.
lines.g_hype: Quiet now, boys and girls, nice and slow. Tegan goes first, we follow her, and nobody shouts until it's time.
lines.g_toast: Not much of a talker, me, but here goes. To all of you, and to Tegan, who's the only one of us who can actually hunt. Iechyd da, everyone.
lines.g_cheers: Cheers, all, and keep it down a bit, mind, she's trying to sleep.
g_quiet_line: Mist on the Beacons first thing, Pen y Fan poking out the top like an island. I'd go up there with Tegan before anybody was awake.
Rain's coming, I can smell it, proper Brecon rain. Tegan hates it, I've always quite liked it.
lines.g_after_wipe: Everyone stay down a second, quietly, nobody jump up. Tegan's on the branch, she's watching, so we're safe for now. Breathe, then slowly up.
lines.g_crew: I never wanted to leave my valley, everyone. Ended up about as far from it as a person can get, and somehow you lot feel like a valley.
lines.g_exasperated: I asked for quiet, three times, in my softest voice. Somebody shouted anyway, and now there isn't a bird left in this whole forest.
lines.g_love_sharp: You spot movement in the trees before Tegan does, {name}, and that's saying a lot.
lines.g_love_kind: You're gentle with the animals, {name}, every one. Tegan's noticed, she lets you close.
lines.g_love_funny: You make me laugh out loud in the woods, {name}, which I never do. Worth scaring a few birds for.
lines.g_love_brave: You walk up to the frightening things calmly, {name}, like you'd walk up to a nervous bird. That's proper courage.
lines.g_love_steady: You're calm, {name}, all the time, and animals love that. I love it too, if I'm allowed to say so.
lines.g_love_clever: You work out what an animal's going to do before it does it, {name}. You'd have been a good falconer.
lines.g_love_honest: You tell people straight, {name}, no fuss. Hawks are the same, and I trust them more than most folk.
lines.g_love_quiet: You can be quiet in the woods without being asked, {name}. Hardly anybody can.
lines.g_love_fierce: You'd fight anything to protect somebody smaller, {name}. Tegan's the same with her chicks, if she had any.
lines.g_love_warm: Being near you is like the cafe at the centre on a wet day, {name}, everybody steaming and laughing.
g_loved: Oh, duw, stop, I'm going red, and Tegan will laugh at me. She does, you know, in her way.
That's kind, cariad, really. Tegan says thank you too, she's just shy about it.
lines.g_hate_sharp: You go after people's weak spots, {name}, like a stoat in a henhouse. Leave it be, please.
lines.g_hate_kind: You keep trying to feed Tegan, {name}. She's on a weight, and you're not helping.
lines.g_hate_funny: Not now, {name}, please, there's something big in those trees. Jokes later, quietly.
lines.g_hate_brave: You crash into the woods without looking, {name}, and every animal hears you coming a mile off.
lines.g_hate_steady: The bird's gone while you're still thinking, {name}. Sometimes you just have to throw the lure.
lines.g_hate_clever: You keep telling me how to fly my hawk, {name}. Fifteen years with birds, and you've had one afternoon.
lines.g_hate_honest: You say every blunt thing the second you think it, {name}. It's like a car horn in a quiet field.
lines.g_hate_quiet: You go cold and quiet and expect me to guess, {name}. I can read a hawk, not you.
lines.g_hate_fierce: Everything's a fight with you, {name}, even putting the tent up. The tent isn't arguing back.
lines.g_hate_warm: You talk all the way through the woods, {name}, every single walk. Tegan's not caught a thing in days.
lines.g_respect: You and I don't click, {name}, and that's allowed. But you held firm in that fight, and Tegan didn't flinch at you once.
lines.g_call_out: That one's on you, {name}, I'm sorry, but it is. You went charging in loud, and we all paid for it.
lines.g_stung: Yeah, fair, I hear you. I'll take Tegan for a walk.
lines.g_concede: You had the right of it, {name}, and I had it wrong. Even Tegan was looking at me like I was daft.
lines.g_nod: Ta, {name}, tidy work. No fuss, mind.
lines.g_callback_save: You got between me and that wolf, {name}, with Tegan on my arm. I don't forget things like that.
lines.g_callback_clutch: You and me upright at the end, everything else down, Tegan screaming at it all. I tell that one quietly, in the woods.
lines.g_callback_callout: When you told me I was too soft with people, I sulked a whole day with the bird. Then I stood up for myself, and you were right.
lines.g_former_rivals: First time I met you, {name}, Tegan wouldn't look at you. Now she leans toward you, and so do I.
lines.g_changed: I used to keep myself to myself, everyone, and the bird. Lately I sit at the fire and talk, and it's nice.
g_unguarded: Between us, cariad. I'm lucky, Tegan came through with me. Most folk lost everything, and I feel guilty about having her.
Just you and me, so I'll say it. I don't know if Brecon came through, and I'm frightened to go and look.
lines.g_clipped: Right, your call. I'll be with the bird.
lines.g_noticed_open: Look at you, telling it all the way through, out loud. Go on, softly, I'm listening.
arg_ask: {player}, would you sort this out, please? Mine's been said quietly, and nobody listens to quiet.
Help us out, {player}, cariad. You decide, and I'll go with it, promise.
lines.arg_backed_me: Ta, {player}, that's kind of you. Tegan agrees, look at her.
lines.arg_backed_them: Right, fair enough, we'll do it that way. It's the loud way, mind.
lines.arg_stayed_out: Keeping out of it, eh? Can't blame you, I'd rather be up the ridge myself.
lines.arg_always_their_side: Tegan's noticed who wins every row, {player}, and so have I, quiet as I am.
lines.arg_wallflower: Nobody's deciding, so I will, softly. My way, and we go.
lines.arg_reject: No, {player}, sorry, I can't do that one. It'd frighten everything for miles.
lines.arg_grumble: Okay, I'll let it lie, mostly. Tegan won't, she holds grudges.
lines.arg_settled: Half each, tidy, fair enough. Shake on it, quietly, please.
lines.seen_listens: Softly, {player}, you wait for quiet ones like me to get to the end. Tegan's noticed, and so have I.
lines.seen_truth: You give people the real answer, {player}, gently but straight. Like a good bird handler, honest about the bird.
lines.seen_jokes: On the rough days the whole camp laughs because of you, {player}. Even Tegan cocks her head.
lines.seen_stays_out: You keep away from the rows, {player}, like a sensible bird on a high branch, and that's wise.
lines.seen_biased: Funny, {player}, how one person ends up with the best kit every trip. Tegan watches who gets fed first, and so do I.
lines.seen_harsh: Careful, {player}, you can be rough with people. Some of them spook easy, like young birds.
lines.seed_right: Remember that advice from the rough day, {player}? I tried it, and it worked, like a bird coming back to the glove.
lines.seed_remember: What you told me when it all went wrong, {player}, they're still circling, like a hawk that won't come down.
lines.seed_wrong: Did it your way, {player}, and it went worse. Only saying, cariad, no hard feelings.
lines.talk_aftermath_near_death: Can you sit with me, {player}, quietly? That one was too close, and Tegan's still shaking on my arm, and so am I.
lines.talk_aftermath_wipe: Every one of us down, and Tegan screaming from the tree. Let's go back through it, softly, nobody blamed.
lines.talk_aftermath_blame_self: Tegan saw it coming before {name} fell, {player}, and I didn't read her in time. That one's on me.
lines.talk_aftermath_first_clear: In and out, everybody walking, Tegan back on the glove. That's a perfect day, {player}, like a show where nothing goes wrong.
lines.talk_development: Odd one, {player}, but have I changed, do you think? I said what I thought at the fire last night, out loud, first.
lines.talk_relationship_hard_on: Duw, {player}, {name}'s had my prickly side lately. Tired, I go quiet and prickly, and they've had the prickly bit.
lines.talk_relationship_likes_me: Tegan likes {name}, {player}, I can tell. Is it me {name} likes, though, or just the bird?
lines.talk_relationship_respect_hate: {name} drives me round the bend, {player}. But in a dark wood, I'd still pick them to walk behind me.
lines.talk_relationship_acting_off: Tegan won't settle near {name} today, {player}. Something's wrong with them, and she can feel it.
lines.talk_confrontation_favour: Quietly, {player}, if I can. {name} picks the kit first, every time. If there's a reason, I'd just like to hear it.
lines.talk_confrontation_dislike: Honest version, {player}. {name} and I don't sit well together, and pretending only makes the woods noisier.
lines.talk_confrontation_risks: We walk into rooms with no way out, {player}. A bird never flies into a room without a window, and nor should we.
lines.talk_confrontation_wrong: My read on {name} was all wrong, {player}. Tegan knew before I did, as usual. They were right.
lines.talk_confrontation_trust: Gently, {player}, a fair question. On the big jobs, me and Tegan stay behind. Is it something about us?
lines.talk_confrontation_decided: My kit's gone to {name}, and I had to find out myself. A question first, {player}, and it was theirs.
lines.talk_lands_aftermath: Ta, {player}, that helps, honest. Want to hold the glove? She won't bite, much.
lines.talk_shrug_aftermath: I'll be all right, cariad, give it a night up the ridge.
lines.talk_stings_aftermath: That didn't help much, sorry. I'll take Tegan for a fly.
lines.talk_lands_development: So it shows, then. That's nice to know, that is.
lines.talk_shrug_development: Maybe, maybe not, hard to tell. Ask Tegan, she knows me better.
lines.talk_stings_development: Nah, that's not it, {player}. You've read me wrong there.
lines.talk_lands_relationship: Fair enough, yeah. {name} and I will have a quiet word, away from the others.
lines.talk_shrug_relationship: Could be, cariad, who knows. Nobody comes with jesses on.
lines.talk_stings_relationship: Forget I said, please. Not a word to {name}, mind.
lines.talk_lands_confrontation: Okay, that's earned. Stings a bit, but it's earned.
lines.talk_shrug_confrontation: I hear you, cariad, and I'll think on it up the ridge.
lines.talk_stings_confrontation: Right, then, message understood. Tegan and I will know where we are.
lines.talk_door_closed: That's enough of that, I think. I'll be with Tegan.
lines.arc_cracks: I unpacked properly last night, {player}, all my things, for the first time since I got here. Felt odd, and quite nice.
lines.arc_turn: I've been living like I'm only passing through, {player}, ready to go home any minute. I don't think home's coming.
lines.arc_become: This is home now, everyone, here, with you lot and Tegan. Brecon's still in me, but I've stopped waiting to leave.
lines.arc_failed: I still keep my pack ready by the door, {player}, every night, just in case, and I can't stop.
lines.alt_turn: I dreamed about the Beacons again, {player}, and woke up thinking I was home. Took me ages to stop crying.
lines.alt_become: I'll keep going, cariad, but my heart's in that valley, and it's not coming out, and I'm sorry for it.
lines.g_roast_after: Still the noisiest party I've ever walked a wood with, boys and girls, and I wouldn't swap one of you.
lines.g_after_wipe_after: Up, slowly, quietly, a hand for whoever's next to you. Nobody stays on the ground alone, Tegan's rules.
lines.g_toast_after: To you lot, my valley now, wherever we are. And to Tegan, who knew before I did.
lines.g_crew_after: This is my home now, everyone, here with you. I've unpacked, and I'm staying unpacked.
g_quiet_line_after: Rain tonight, and for once it doesn't make me homesick. Just makes me want a brew with you lot.
Tegan stayed on the perch by the fire till morning. She only does that when she feels safe.
g_loved_after: Ta, cariad, and I believe it, which is new for me.
That's lovely, that is, and I'll keep it. Tegan's keeping it too.

history.open: Mind your hands near her, {player}, she's deciding about you. This is Tegan, a Harris's hawk. She was on my glove at the falconry centre outside Brecon the evening everything changed, and she came through with me.

options.reply: She hasn't decided yet, cariad. That's her watching you, very carefully. I trust her opinion more than mine, and she's never wrong.
She knows, mind, don't tell her too often. But yes, she is, and she's the best hunter I've ever flown.
Duw, no, please don't say that near her. She's a partner, she chooses to come back to the glove. That's the whole of falconry.

history.open: I'm teaching a tauren boy from Sun Rock to hold a glove, {player}. He's better at it than I was at his age, and he's twice my size, and he talks to the birds in his own language.

options.reply: Not yet, he's learning patience first. That's most of it, the waiting. He's getting good at it, slowly.
Ah, I don't know, I just do what the birds taught me. Be quiet, be patient, and let them choose you.

history.open: My dad died when I was eleven, {player}. He was a shepherd up on the Beacons, and he used to take me out to watch the buzzards. That's where the birds started, really, with him.

options.reply: I hope so, cariad. I think he'd love Tegan. He'd have said she was showing off, and he'd be right.
Quiet, like me, and funny when you didn't expect it. He could whistle a buzzard down. I never learned that one.

friend.open: My mam, Gwen, ran the cafe at the falconry centre, {player}. She took the job after Dad died so we'd manage, and that's how I ended up with the birds. Everything good I've got came out of her doing that. I don't know if Brecon came through.

options.reply: Would you really? I've been too frightened to go and look on my own. With you, maybe I could.
She is, cariad, she's the best. Her Welsh cakes were the best thing in the whole of Powys.

sworn.open: Tegan's decided about you, {player}. She leans in when you walk up, and she's only ever done that for me. So I've decided too. You're family, mind, mine and hers.

options.reply: Tidy, that's settled, then. She'll let you hold the glove now, properly.
Ha, she heard you, look at her. You've said the right thing to the right one.

reconciled.open: {name} and I had a quiet word and sorted it out, {player}. All good now, and I wanted you to hear it from me.

options.reply: Ta, it feels lighter. Tegan's happier too, she always knows.
She did, she let them stroke her, which is the highest honour she gives.
